_help: One entry per recording. hesitations = how many um/uh/ah sounds you really made, counted as one group. fillers = your count of each other filler word. reference = the words you said, optional (it enables the word-mistake score). Use null for anything you haven't counted yet. pauses = how many silent gaps of 2 seconds or more you left on purpose. restarts = how many times you repeated a phrase.

clips.note: Scripted running speech, 60 s. Counts come from the script, so confirm them by listening. The recording auto-stopped after 'best decision', so the reference stops there too.
clips.reference: So, I want to talk about why I started running. Um, a year ago I was, uh, honestly so tired all the time. Basically, I sat at a desk for ten hours a day. So I decided to try something small. I I went outside for, like, ten minutes. It looked like rain, but I went anyway. Uh, the first week was hard, you know, my legs hurt and I felt like quitting. But actually, something changed. Um, I started to like the quiet mornings. I actually slept better, and, uh, my head felt clearer. Do you know what surprised me most? It wasn't the fitness. It was, like, the habit itself. So now I run three times a week, um, and I honestly think it's the best decision

clips.reference: I think the best advice I got at work was, ah, to write things down. Early on I kept everything in my head, and, um, honestly that was a mistake. So my manager told me, like, just keep a simple notes file. It looked like extra work at first, but it actually saved me hours. Now every meeting I take notes, and ahh, I send a short summary afterwards. Basically, it makes me look organised, you know, even on a bad day. Uh, I would tell anyone starting out to try it.
